metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Utah (2026): Rules, Exemptions & Ex.

description: Utah has a statewide sales tax, but investment-grade bullion and legal-tender coins are fully exempt; jewelry and most collectibles are taxed. Statewide rule.

What's covered by the exemption
Gold, silver, and other precious-metal bullion; legal-tender coins
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Utah.
Is bullion taxable in Utah?
+
No. Utah exempts qualifying precious-metal bullion from sales tax under its investment-grade treatment.
Are legal-tender gold and silver coins taxed in Utah?
+
No. Legal-tender coins covered by Utah’s rules are treated as exempt.
Do I pay sales tax on numismatic coins in Utah?
+
Sometimes. Utah’s exemption focuses on qualifying bullion and legal-tender coins, so nonqualifying collectibles can be taxable.
Is precious-metal jewelry taxed in Utah?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable even if it is made of gold or silver.
